title: hosted-api-silent-deadlock-unwind-and-client-guidance
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: Production reports from 3 large customers showed a recurrent class of requests that would hang during streaming responses and ultimately surface as 5xx/timeouts after many client retries. Unlike classic retry-amplification incidents, these calls entered a low-volume, low-telemetry state (no obvious CPU, but increasing goroutine stacks on runtime nodes) — we labeled it a 'silent deadlock'.

Scope & impact: >50 tenants across multiple regions observed elevated tail latency and ~2% request error increases during escalations that triggered aggressive client-side retry logic. Both Hosted and Dedicated frontends saw the pattern; Private customers were less affected but reported diagnostic traces consistent with the same kernel.

Goal: Implement a rapid, low-risk mitigation to break in-flight deadlocks, supply customer-facing guidance to stop harmful retry amplification, and deliver a code fix that removes the root cause from the serving runtime.

Root cause (working theory): A race between the streaming multiplexor and the KV-cache compaction path where slow eviction callbacks could block the multiplexor's response loop under specific timing (large multipart payload + KV eviction triggered mid-stream). The blocked loop prevented the response from flushing headers, leaving client SDKs to assume the request is slow and retry; retries accumulate and exacerbate the blocked path, eventually causing OOM-like scheduling stalls and 5xx results.

Mitigation plan:
1) Immediate mitigation (hotpatch): Add a non-blocking eviction path for in-flight streams and introduce a 250ms soft-flush watchdog in the streaming mux that forces an early partial response and a controlled fast-fail for affected requests. This is scoped to Hosted and Dedicated runtime nodes only and will be gated by rollout flags.
2) Customer guidance: Send triage note to affected customers with temporary SDK guidance to reduce retry aggressiveness (increase base backoff, cap concurrent retries to 2) and to enable SDK idempotency tokens. Provide a simple curl example showing a safe retry pattern.
3) Medium-term: Make KV eviction callbacks asynchronous, add per-connection compaction budgeting, and widen observability on goroutine stacks and eviction latency percentiles.
4) Long-term: Rework streaming multiplexor to use an append-only flush queue to eliminate synchronous eviction contention and add a safe-guarded admission controller to stop retry storms.

Rollback & rollout: Hotpatch will be rolled out to 10% nodes for 30m, then 50% for 1h, then global if no regressions. Rollout flag control is in console-ops and can be toggled per-region. If error rate increases or unusual memory growth is observed, auto-rollback will trigger and ops will notify customers.

Metrics to watch: per-node goroutine count, streaming-mux-wait-latency (p50/p95/p99), kv-eviction-duration p99, tenant error-rate, retry-amplification ratio (retries/initial-requests), memory RSS. Dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/streams/streaming-ops (internal), and a temporary incident dashboard at https://dashboards.redwood.internal/incident/ENG-888202.

Testing: Unit tests for async eviction + end-to-end harness with synthetic multipart uploads (varying chunk sizes) and a scaled load test simulating client retry patterns. Canary includes integration tests with SDKs (Python/Go/Node) to ensure error surfaces are unchanged semantically and contain idempotency token hints.

Communication: Drafted customer escalation template and ready-to-send triage note. PM will coordinate a targeted outreach to top 10 impacted tenants with recommended SDK config.

Deliverables: Hotpatch PR, runtime-2.7.3 canary, SDK guidance doc, postmortem with timeline and follow-ups.
